title: Unify signed SDK publish pipeline and sample SDK release examples
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Problem: Our three SDK ecosystems (Python, TypeScript, Go) each have slightly different publish flows, signature formats, and sample-release examples. This causes confusion for maintainers, flaky CI across registries (PyPI/npm/godoc), and gaps in verifiable provenance for released artifacts. We also have duplicate sample apps that demonstrate streaming, retry, and backpressure ergonomics; they are lagging behind the canonical SDK behavior and frequently fail during publish canaries. Goal: Provide a single, documented pipeline that produces signed, registry-ready artifacts for Python, TS, and Go; rotates signing keys safely; publishes reproducible example releases; and surfaces deterministic verification steps for customers and auditors. Scope: 1) CI changes to unify build matrix (python wheel + sdist, npm package, go module zip) and canonicalize versioning semantics (semantic version bump hook and changelog generation). 2) Add mandatory artifact signatures using cosign for container/artifact blobs and GPG detached sigs for PyPI wheels, with a verifiable bundle stored in an S3-backed release-proof bucket (immutable, versioned). 3) Update sample SDK example apps that exercise streaming responses, client-side retries, and streaming ergonomics so they are republishable as 3 language-specific example releases. 4) Provide documented verification steps and a lightweight verifier script (cosign + GPG + checksum) that customers can run. 5) Key rotation plan and emergency rollback playbook for compromised signing keys. Out of scope: Full in-toto attestation integration (deferred to follow-up), cross-repo SBOM standardization (separate initiative). Acceptance criteria: - Single CI pipeline job (or composite job) named "sdk/publish/unified" that outputs python, npm, and go artifacts and uploads signed artifacts to the release bucket. - All three SDKs publishable from CI to staging registries with detached signature files attached. - Example releases (python-examples v0.1.0, ts-examples v0.1.0, go-examples v0.1.0) in staging with passing smoke tests that exercise streaming + retries. - Documentation page "SDK release verification" in Confluence with step-by-step verification and key fingerprints. - Key rotation runbook committed to repo and validated in a dry-run. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: Registry rate limits and account throttles during end-to-end integration. Mitigation: Use per-registry staging accounts and token quota; add retries with exponential backoff and idempotent publish steps. - Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: Short-lived keys for CI (cosign ephemeral), offline master key in HSM with human approval for urgent re-sign. - Risk: Example fragmentation — sample apps drift away from SDKs. Mitigation: Add CI checks that run example smoke tests against released SDK packages and treat failures as blocking. Rollout plan: Week 1 (2026-03-02 to 2026-03-08): design doc + CI job prototype, pick signing technology (cosign + GPG), and create release bucket. Week 2: wire up publish job for PyPI and npm to staging, attach GPG/cosign signatures. Week 3: add go module packaging and example releases; run cross-language smoke tests. Week 4: documentation, key rotation dry-run, security review, and production rollout to the live registries. Monitoring & QA: - Add per-job artifacts stored in CI for replay (build logs, checksums, signature files). - Add synthetic smoke tests that exercise streaming generation and retry parameters (simulate transient failures and assert graceful retry behavior). - Add dashboard card in Console for publish job success rate and time-to-publish. Documentation & training: - Confluence how-to for maintainers: publish checklist, key rotation steps, troubleshooting. - Short walkthrough session with SDK maintainers and on-call team.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: Chosen cosign for container/artifact signing and GPG for wheel signatures. Security approved evaluating cosign ephemeral keys for CI and keeping long-term root in HSM.

2026-03-03 — Prototype CI created: .github/workflows/sdk-unified-publish.yml with python build and wheel signing. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2345. Observed PyPI test.pypi.org upload succeeded but metadata mismatch for sdist name — fixed setup.cfg version template.
2026-03-04 — Design review: Marco Chen (Infra) requested per-registry tokens be stored in vault with lease TTL and vault-agent sidecar for CI runners. Added to CI changes.

2026-03-05 — Design decision: Go modules will be published by tagging the example repo and pushing a release zip; npm will use npm dist-tag staging to avoid purging. Liam added a publish-canary flag to skip pushing to production registries.

2026-03-06 — Implemented example smoke tests that run a streaming echo server and validate client-side streaming chunk handling + retry backoff. Tests pass locally but flaky on GH-hosted runners due to network variance; creating dedicated integration runner (self-hosted) with stable egress.

2026-03-07 — Security review notes from Priya Khatri: require signed release manifest (SHA256 list) and include cosign sigs in release bucket. Also requested a hardening checklist for GPG keys (expiration, subkey rotations). Added to runbook.

2026-03-09 — PR review feedback: split the pipeline into 3 parallel build matrices to avoid long-runner locks. Also add an explicit checksum verification step before publishing. Liam pushed commit to the PR addressing both items and re-ran CI: all artifacts built, signatures attached, and staging publish succeeded.
2026-03-10 — Next: schedule dry-run key rotation on 2026-03-18, prepare Confluence verification doc, and coordinate a short demo for SDK maintainers on 2026-03-16.
next_steps: Complete dry-run key rotation and confirm revoke path works as expected
Finish Confluence verification guide and add explicit command examples for cosign + GPG verification
Migrate existing per-language publish jobs into composite sdk/publish/unified CI job and retire old jobs
Coordinate demo and handoff to SDK maintainers
